findings.title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, a likely leftover debug change
findings.body: The cleanup service ticker went from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. The PR description does not mention or justify this. Every cleanup job (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, annotations, user invites, short URLs, and the query-history row-limit enforcement) now runs 10x more often, which multiplies background DB load on every installation. The 9-minute `timeout` in `clean()` was sized to fit inside the 10-minute interval, so with a 1-minute ticker that relationship no longer holds. This looks like a local-testing change and should be reverted.

findings.title: Leftover debug logging at Error level dumps full ID lists on every batch
findings.body: `CleanAnnotations` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557) and `CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags` (lines 576, 579) call `r.log.Error` on every batch, including successful ones and empty ones. Each call logs the whole `ids` slice, which can hold up to `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` entries (tens of thousands), plus the SQL condition. Every cleanup run therefore emits several Error-level lines per annotation type even when nothing is deleted. That floods logs and trips error-based alerting. The `"err", err` field in the fetch log is always nil at that point, which further suggests this is debug code. These lines should be removed or downgraded to Debug without the ID list.

findings.title: Quadratic string building when inlining IDs for SQLite
findings.body: The SQLite inline path builds the IN list with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` in a loop. Each iteration reallocates and copies the whole growing string, so the cost is O(n²). With a large batch size such as the 32767 used in the new test, this copies gigabytes of data and adds heavy GC pressure on every batch. A `strings.Builder` or `strconv.AppendInt` into a `[]byte` would make it linear, as `getAccessControlFilter` already does in this file.

findings.title: Bound-parameter limit is now a hard cap on batch size for MySQL/Postgres
findings.body: The old cleanup used a single subquery with no bound parameters, so `annotation_cleanup_job_batch_size` had no upper limit. `deleteByIDs` now binds one placeholder per ID on every non-SQLite database. MySQL prepared statements and Postgres both reject more than 65535 parameters. A user with a batch size above that will see every cleanup run fail and annotations never get cleaned. Either chunk the delete or inline integer IDs for all dialects, since they are int64 values read from the DB and safe to inline.

findings.title: Per-subtest DB cleanup is registered only after setup assertions succeed
findings.body: All subtests share one DB. `t.Cleanup` (which deletes from `annotation` and `annotation_tag`) is registered only after `createTestAnnotations`, `assertAnnotationCount` and `assertAnnotationTagCount` have run, and those helpers call `require`. If any of them fails partway, for example after some rows were inserted, the cleanup is never registered. The leftover rows then make every later subtest fail with misleading counts. Registering the cleanup before creating test data avoids these cascading failures.
